history.summary: CSV town correction: 'Rajahmundry' is the anglicized name of Rajamahendravaram, the same city — town corrected to the official name Rajamahendravaram. The temple is the Sri Uma Kotilingeswara Swamy temple on the Koti Lingala Ghat ('crore-lingas revu') on the banks of the Godavari in Rajamahendravaram, about 4.7 km north of the city centre, with Sri Rama as kshetrapalaka and seven upalayas in the premises. The site doubles as the Godavari Tir Shakti Peeth (Sarvashail), where Sati's left cheek is said to have fallen; Shakti is worshipped as Vishweshwari/Rakini with Bhairava as Dandapani/Vatsnabha. Two caution flags: (1) Wikipedia's 'Kotilingam' article appears to conflate this Rajahmundry temple with a different Kotilingam temple at Panchadharla (Visakhapatnam), so its mention of 15th-century inscriptions should not be assumed to belong to this shrine; (2) one travel source claims a 108-foot Shivalinga as 'tallest of its kind in the world' — this is unverified. No reliable account of the temple's founding dynasty or date was found.

name: Sri Uma Kotilingeswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Rajamahendravaram (formerly Rajahmundry) is a historic city in East Godavari district on the eastern bank of the Godavari river, often called the cultural capital of Andhra Pradesh. Its ghats along the river — including the Koti Lingala Ghat — are major pilgrimage spots, especially during the Godavari Pushkaram held every twelve years, and the city has its own airport and railway station.

travel.road: At the Koti Lingala Ghat, approx. 4.7 km north of the city centre and approx. 4 km from the bus stand; autos and taxis readily available.

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter) is the best season; the 12-yearly Godavari Pushkaram draws millions.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listing shows approx. 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM daily (verify — timings not confirmed by an official source). Modest traditional dress; bathing at the ghat is part of the visit.
